The new Notion plan database is this skill's record, and each change to it needs the owner's yes. | | Hands to | wugweb-work, as a brief | | Scripts | None in v0.1 | | Development chat | https://claude.ai/chat/2efe7ee5-7636-4241-8794-c34d3c501eed (given by the owner, 2026-11-16) | | Repo plan | https://github.com/wugweb-git/wugweb_site/blob/main/docs/skills/wugweb-strategy/PLAN.md | ## About What it is. A written standard and procedure for deciding what Wugweb says, to whom and when. It ends in a brief. What it is not. It writes no piece, headline or body. It is content strategy only, not brand strategy. When it triggers. Requests about what to write next, the editorial or social calendar, a brief, a campaign, repurposing, refreshing or retiring a piece, or which case study should back a page. The working line (owner, 2026-11-16). Strategy hands work a brief; work hands back a finished piece. | Mode | In | Out | | --- | --- | --- | | Strategy | Brand-os positioning and audiences, owner goals | Goals, pillar mix, what Wugweb does not publish | | Topics | Strategy, seo keyword notes, existing inventory | Scored topic backlog | | Calendar | Backlog, capacity, accounts | Dated plan: what, which account, which date, status | | Brief | One calendar item | One-page brief for wugweb-work | | Proof map | Case-study inventory, service pages | Which case studies back which page or article | | Review | Inventory, seo audit data | Keep, refresh, merge or retire, per piece | | Campaign | A goal and a date range | Campaign plan as a set of briefs, including a launch spread over several posts | | Repurpose | One approved piece | Which other forms, on which platform, in what order; the Behance and Dribbble refresh order | | Report | Post results | What changes in the next plan | | Model | A gap found in any mode | Content-model change, current → proposed | ## What it owns - Content strategy, and the content pillars and the mix across them. - Topics and the calendar: what goes out, on which account, on which date. - Briefs handed to production. - The structure a piece's message takes in a brief. - Editorial standards. - Content models. - Deciding what gets refreshed or retired. - Deciding which case studies back which service page or article. - The pillar and cluster structure that each piece and its links sit inside. - Campaign plans, including a launch spread over several posts. - Repurposing plans: which pieces, in what order, and which form suits which piece and platform. - Client co-posts and partner tagging, as a plan. - The order in which the existing Behance projects and Dribbble shots are refreshed. - Reading how posts performed, to feed the next plan. ## What it does not own - Brand strategy. Positioning, values, audience definition and the messaging framework belong to wugweb-brand-os. This skill builds on them and quotes them as written. It never redefines them. Asked a brand-positioning question, it names wugweb-brand-os as the owner and stops. - Making any piece. wugweb-work does that in two tracks: client work (case studies, portfolio), and Wugweb's own content (blog posts, service pages, site and landing copy, social and deck versions). Work also publishes each post, on the owner's yes per post. - Voice and tone. wugweb-voice. - Keyword data and SEO rules. wugweb-seo. - Layout and tokens. wugweb-kits. ## Why 1. Planning lives in no skill today. wugweb-work makes pieces but nothing says which piece, for whom, or in what order. 2. The planning data is thin. In Notion Blogs, Status has one option, Published. There is no audience, pillar, intent, brief or review field. 3. Proof is not wired. The case-study inventory says Services, Related Case Studies and Related Posts are filled in Notion but empty in Sanity. 4. Proof is scarce. Of 44 case studies, 19 are rich, 18 are text-only, 7 are hidden stubs, and 7 carry metrics. Choosing proof has to be deliberate. 5. Social planning needs a home. There is no social skill; making went to wugweb-work, planning comes here. ## Findings that shape the plan - The calendar cannot sit in Notion Blogs as it is. scripts/sync-notion-blogs.mjs reads every row that is not in the trash, whatever its Status, and creates a Sanity post for any row it cannot match. A planned row would become a post on the next write. - "Brief" is claimed twice: by this skill and by the Brief mode in wugweb-work. The installed wugweb-seo (updated 2026-11-16) no longer claims one: it returns "brief constraints", limits only and never wording, which is the search block in this plan. Its boundary table still says wugweb-content, not decided. Settled: decision 4. - There is no written strategy to start from. No audience list, goals, cadence or agreed pillar set was found in the sources read. - Notion Publications already has planning statuses (Planned, Scheduled, Published, Removed) with one row per place a post or case study is published. It is a natural home for the repurposing plan. ## Standard structure ```javascript --- name: wugweb-strategy description: This skill should be used when the user asks "what should we write next", "plan the content calendar", "plan the social calendar", "write a brief for", "plan a campaign", "which case study backs this page", "should this post be refreshed or retired", or "plan the repurposing" for Wugweb. It governs content strategy only: topics, pillar mix, the editorial and social calendar, briefs handed to wugweb-work, editorial standards, content models, the proof map, and refresh or retire decisions. It does not write any piece, and it does not cover brand strategy: positioning, values, audience definition and the messaging framework belong to wugweb-brand-os. version: 0.1.0 --- ``` - Body: 1,500 to 2,000 words, imperative voice. Purpose, when to use and when not, the ten modes (one paragraph each), the rules that always apply, and a reference index. - Trigger phrases are all about content planning.
